# stalwart_sieve_system_interpreter (Data Source)

Configures the system-level Sieve script interpreter settings and limits. This singleton object always exists: creating the resource adopts the current server settings and destroying it only removes the resource from state.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `default_from_address` (Attributes) Default email address to use for the from field in email notifications sent from a Sieve script (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_from_address))
- `default_from_name` (Attributes) Default name to use for the from field in email notifications sent from a Sieve script (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_from_name))
- `default_return_path` (Attributes) Default return path to use in email notifications sent from a Sieve script (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_return_path))
- `dkim_sign_domain` (Attributes) Which domain's DKIM signatures to use when signing the email notifications sent from a Sieve script (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dkim_sign_domain))
- `duplicate_expiry` (Number) Default expiration time for IDs stored by the duplicate extension from trusted scripts
- `id` (String) Always `singleton`.
- `max_cpu_cycles` (Number) Maximum number CPU cycles a script can use
- `max_nested_includes` (Number) Maximum number of nested includes
- `max_out_messages` (Number) Maximum number of outgoing messages
- `max_received_headers` (Number) Maximum number of received headers
- `max_redirects` (Number) Maximum number of redirects
- `max_var_size` (Number) Maximum size of a variable
- `message_id_hostname` (String) Override the default local hostname to use when generating a Message-Id header
- `no_capability_check` (Boolean) If enabled, language extensions can be used without being explicitly declared using the require statement
